careers.title: Software Developer
careers.description: Designs, builds, and maintains software systems and digital products.
careers.role_description: Design, build, test and maintain web applications and backend services. Day to day: reading requirements, writing code, reviewing pull requests, fixing defects.
daily_work: Turn a short requirements note into working code
Review a teammate's pull request over coffee
Fix a bug reported by a tester or a user
Pair with someone on a tricky bit of logic
Write or run tests so tomorrow's change stays safe

related.rationale: You already build networked systems; pivoting shifts the goal from shipping features to defending them.
SQL and structured thinking transfer directly. You would trade writing services for querying data.
Front-end work puts you close to interface decisions even without a design background.
A build-adjacent route that leans on requirements and communication rather than code.

careers.title: Cybersecurity Analyst
careers.description: Protects systems, networks, and data from threats and vulnerabilities.
careers.role_description: Monitor systems, investigate incidents and harden infrastructure against threats.
daily_work: Read overnight alerts and triage what matters
Investigate a suspicious login or a misconfigured rule
Patch or harden a server and document the change
Run a vulnerability scan and write up the findings
Brief a non-technical team on what to watch for

related.rationale: Building experience plus your defence lens makes platform and tooling work a natural sideways move.
Security work is mostly written communication: findings, risk, and the fix you are asking for.

careers.title: Data Analyst
careers.description: Turns raw data into insight through analysis, visualization, and reporting.
careers.role_description: Clean and query data, build reports and dashboards, and brief stakeholders.
daily_work: Pull and clean a messy export from a source system
Write queries to answer a plain business question
Build a chart that makes the trend obvious
Sanity-check numbers with the person who owns them
Write a short summary of what the data says

related.rationale: Analysis experience is the strongest predictor of success in a business analyst role.
Your SQL and structured thinking transfer straight into writing and querying services.
Campaign reporting leans on the same query, chart and story skills you already use.

careers.title: Business Analyst
careers.description: Bridges business needs and technical solutions through structured analysis.
careers.role_description: Document processes, gather requirements and translate business needs into solutions.
daily_work: Interview the people who do the actual work
Map a process and spot where it breaks down
Write requirements a developer can act on
Facilitate a meeting between two teams that talk past each other
Check the delivered change against the original need

related.rationale: A data-first route with less stakeholder facilitation and more time in the query editor.
A build-adjacent route that leans on your requirements and communication skills.
Both jobs turn a fuzzy request into a plan other people can execute.

careers.title: UI/UX Designer
careers.description: Creates usable, accessible digital experiences through research and design.
careers.role_description: Research user needs, design interfaces and prototypes, and validate with users.
daily_work: Watch a student try the screen you just designed
Sketch three versions of a flow before choosing one
Build a clickable prototype and tighten the spacing
Pair with a developer on what is actually buildable
Run an accessibility pass on the finished screen

related.rationale: A design route without the research and prototyping load.
Interface decisions sit right next to implementation, so design and code can feed each other.
Screens are mostly words and hierarchy — content thinking makes the design stronger.

careers.title: Graphic Designer
careers.description: Communicates ideas visually through typography, layout, and imagery.
careers.role_description: Create visual assets for brand, print and digital channels.
daily_work: Take a one-line brief and sketch a few directions
Set type, colour and layout for a poster or a post
Prepare files for print or for the web
Present the work and take feedback without taking it personally
Keep a messy asset folder tidy and on brand

related.rationale: Visual fundamentals transfer; you would add interaction patterns and user research.
Editorial direction and visual execution usually travel in the same team.
Campaigns need the assets you make and the eye you have for them.

careers.title: Content Strategist
careers.description: Plans and produces content that reaches and resonates with target audiences.
careers.role_description: Plan content calendars and editorial direction across channels.
daily_work: Decide what gets written this month and why
Brief a writer (or write it yourself) against a goal
Edit for clarity, tone, and the keyword you care about
Schedule and publish across two or three channels
Check what performed and adjust the plan

related.rationale: Content is the input to campaign work; marketing owns the distribution and measurement.
Editorial direction and visual execution usually travel in the same team.
Product screens are mostly words and hierarchy — content thinking makes the design stronger.

careers.title: Marketing Specialist
careers.description: Promotes products and brands through research, campaigns, and channels.
careers.role_description: Run campaigns, analyse channel performance and grow awareness.
daily_work: Set up a campaign and its audience segments
Write or review the copy that goes out
Watch the numbers and shift budget mid-week
Talk to design about the next set of assets
Write a short recap of what worked and what did not

related.rationale: A communications-first route with less focus on paid channels.
Campaign reporting leans on the same query, chart and story skills.
Campaigns need the assets you make and the eye you have for them.
